I don't actually think it's particularly useful to specifically discuss ways to commit suicide, I was just after a catchy title.

But I did want to discuss whether people view direct suicide, i.e. gun to the head, similarly to killing oneself indirectly through drugs, alcohol, smoking, risky sports, and so on.

If you take the view that you forfeit the right to suicide if you have children, for example, do you also forfeit the right to do anything that puts your life in immediate danger (say, base jumping) or could drastically shorten your life (smoking, heavy drinking, being overweight, etc).
Six million ways to die -- choose one

This goes without saying, but I think it would boil down to intent. Obviously the more common behaviors like drug abuse and risky activities are self destructive, but a person's purpose might not be self destruction while doing those things. I think anyone has the right to live how they choose, but that comes at the cost of the right of others to judge you.

*edit - Also, just to get some of the stigma removed, when the time comes, I plan on using a helium exit bag, with a backup shotgun... if fate doesn't take me out first.

D'you know, I'm not sure I agree with you. If you take a view that a parent killing themselves is inconsiderate, there has to be strong argument that the parent who puts their life in unnecessary danger is inconsiderate too. I guess it also raises questions about men that have children in their 70s or people that have children and do dangerous job (armed forces, for example).

I don't agree it boils down to intent, because then anyone can absolve themselves from parental duties by claiming they "didn't mean to". Could I die with a clear conscience by getting blind drunk and going out for a drive? I wouldn't be doing it with the intention of killing myself but there's a good chance something bad is going to happen.

This is probably a more appropriate debate for a parenting forum, but I think it would be easy for a suicidal parent to rationalise that killing themselves isn't much worse that eating, smoking or drinking themselves to an early grave. Whether or not it's the purpose, if I do something with the knowledge that it could leave my children fatherless, I may just as well go jump off a cliff.
